chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And mention Allah during the numbered days.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'These are the days of Al-Tashreeq. When they stayed in Mina after the sacrifice, they would boast, and one of them would say, 'My father used to do such and such.'
So Allah, Majestic is His Praise, said: 'Then when you depart from Arafat, mention Allah as you mentioned your fathers, or with a greater mention.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the Takbeer is: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no god except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. Allah is the Greatest. And for Allah is the Praise. Allah is the Greatest upon what He has guided us. Allah is the Greatest upon what He has graced us with from the beasts of the livestock.'

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: The Days of Al-Tashreeq (11th-13th Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.عَرَفاتٍ: Arafat (the plain where pilgrims stand during Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific formula for Takbeer during the Days of Al-Tashreeq according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi elucidates the 'numbered days' of Surah Al-Baqarah as the Days of Tashreeq, highlighting a shift from the pre-Islamic practice of ancestral boasting to a superior, divine remembrance. It prescribes the specific liturgical formula for Takbeer, emphasizing gratitude for guidance and sustenance, which underscores the Shia emphasis on ritual precision and spiritual introspection during the Hajj season.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:203] And mention Allah during the numbered days. Heasws said: ‘These are the days of Al-Tashreek (11th, 12th & 13th Zilhajj). It was so that whenever they (the people) stayed in Mina after the sacrifice, used to pride (over others). So the man among them would say, ‘My father used to do such and such’.
So Allahazwj, Majestic is Hisazwj Praise, Said (When you have departed from Arafaat) [2:200] then mention Allah as you mentioned your forefathers, rather with a greater mention.

Heasws said: ‘And the exclamation of the Takbeer is - ‘Allahazwj is the Greatest (beyond description)! Allahazwj is the Greatest (beyond description)! There is no god except for Allahazwj, and Allahazwj is the Greatest (beyond description). Allahazwj is the Greatest (beyond description). And for Allahazwj is the Praise. Allahazwj is the Greatest (beyond description) upon what Allahazwj having Guided us. Allahazwj is the Greatest (beyond description) upon having Graced us over the animals, the cattle’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, ‘Speak of Allah during the well identified days’ [2:203] has said, ‘Such days are the bright days, 11, 12 and 13 of Dhu al-Hajjah. The Arabs would stay in Mina’ after the tenth of Dhu al-Hajjah and speak of their superiority over the others. A man among them would say, ‘My father did such and such things.’
Allah, the most Blessed, the most High, then said, ‘When you leave ‘Arafat, speak of Allah just as you speak of your fathers or even more intensely.’ (2:198-200)

He (the Imam) then said, ‘Takbirat are as follows. ‘Allahu Akbar (Allah is great beyond description), Allahu Akbar (Allah is great beyond description). No one deserves worship except Allah, Allahu Akbar (Allah is great beyond description), Allahu Akbar (Allah is great beyond description). All praise belongs to Allah, Allahu Akbar (Allah is great beyond description), for His granting us guidance, Allahu Akbar (Allah is great beyond description) for His giving us cattle.’”
